name: Unencrypted HTTP Endpoint
description: Unencrypted HTTP Endpoint — §164.312(e)(1) — Transmission Security.
recommendation: Replace http:// with https:// for all external endpoints. ePHI in transit must be encrypted.

name: TLS Verification Disabled
description: TLS Verification Disabled — §164.312(e)(1) — Transmission Security.
recommendation: Never disable TLS certificate verification. Disabling it exposes ePHI to man-in-the-middle attacks.

name: Weak Randomness in Security Context
description: Weak Randomness in Security Context — §164.312(d) — Person Authentication.
recommendation: Use secrets.token_hex() or secrets.token_urlsafe() for session tokens and authentication values.

name: Potential SQL Injection
description: Potential SQL Injection — §164.312(a)(1) — Access Control.
recommendation: Use parameterized queries. SQL injection on a patient database constitutes unauthorized ePHI access.

name: Potential PHI in Logs
description: Potential PHI in Logs — §164.312(b) — Audit Controls.
recommendation: Do not log raw patient data. Log event types and record IDs only; mask or omit PHI fields entirely.

name: Insecure Deserialization (Pickle)
description: Insecure Deserialization (Pickle) — §164.312(c)(1) — Integrity.
recommendation: pickle.loads() on untrusted data enables arbitrary code execution, risking complete ePHI compromise.

name: Hardcoded Healthcare API Credential
description: Hardcoded Healthcare API Credential — §164.308(a)(1) — Security Management Process.
recommendation: Healthcare integration credentials must be stored in environment variables or a secrets manager.

name: Hardcoded JWT / Auth Secret
description: Hardcoded JWT / Auth Secret — §164.312(d) — Person Authentication.
recommendation: JWT secrets loaded from source code allow authentication bypass. Use environment variables or a vault.

name: Debug Mode Enabled
description: Debug Mode Enabled — §164.308(a)(1) — Security Management Process.
recommendation: Disable debug mode before deployment. Stack traces and verbose errors may expose ePHI.

name: Database Connection Without Encryption Flag
description: Database Connection Without Encryption Flag — §164.312(e)(1) — Transmission Security.
recommendation: Add SSL/TLS parameters to database URLs (e.g., ?sslmode=require) to encrypt ePHI in transit.

name: Weak Password Hashing Algorithm
description: Weak Password Hashing Algorithm — §164.312(d) — Person Authentication.
recommendation: MD5 and SHA-1 are cryptographically broken for password storage. Use bcrypt, argon2, or scrypt via passlib.

name: CORS Wildcard Origin
description: CORS Wildcard Origin — §164.312(a)(1) — Access Control.
recommendation: A wildcard CORS origin allows any domain to call your API. Restrict to a known allow-list of trusted origins.

name: Insecure Session Cookie
description: Insecure Session Cookie — §164.312(e)(1) — Transmission Security.
recommendation: Session cookies must set Secure=True and HttpOnly=True to prevent ePHI session tokens from being stolen.

name: S3 Bucket Public-Read ACL
description: S3 Bucket Public-Read ACL — §164.312(a)(1) — Access Control.
recommendation: Public S3 ACLs expose all stored objects to the internet. Use private ACLs with pre-signed URLs for authorized access to ePHI.

name: Hardcoded SSN in Source
description: Hardcoded SSN in Source — §164.308(a)(1) — Security Management Process.
recommendation: Social Security Numbers must not appear in source code or test fixtures. Use synthetic or de-identified test data.

name: Unparameterized NoSQL Query
description: Unparameterized NoSQL Query — §164.312(a)(1) — Access Control.
recommendation: User-controlled input injected into NoSQL queries can bypass access controls on ePHI. Use schema validation and sanitization.

name: Plaintext ePHI Written to Disk
description: Plaintext ePHI Written to Disk — §164.312(e)(2) — Encryption.
recommendation: ePHI written to disk must be encrypted at rest. Use encrypted storage or apply AES-256 encryption before writing.

name: Cardholder PAN in Source Code
description: Cardholder PAN in Source Code — PCI-DSS Req 3.4 — Stored Cardholder Data.
recommendation: Primary Account Numbers must never appear in source code. Use tokenization or masked test surrogates.

name: CVV/CVC Storage
description: CVV/CVC Storage — PCI-DSS Req 3.3 — Prohibited Data.
recommendation: CVV/CVC codes must never be stored after authorization. Storage is prohibited regardless of encryption.

name: Magnetic Stripe Track Data
description: Magnetic Stripe Track Data — PCI-DSS Req 3.3 — Prohibited Data.
recommendation: Magnetic stripe track data must never be stored after authorization. Remove storage and retention code entirely.

name: Unencrypted Payment Endpoint
description: Unencrypted Payment Endpoint — PCI-DSS Req 4.2 — Transmission Security.
recommendation: All cardholder data transmission must use TLS 1.2+. Replace http:// with https:// on all payment endpoints.

name: Prohibited Weak Cipher
description: Prohibited Weak Cipher — PCI-DSS Req 4.2 — Transmission Security.
recommendation: DES, 3DES, and RC4 are prohibited for protecting cardholder data. Use AES-256 with GCM or CBC+HMAC.

name: Hardcoded Payment Processor Credential
description: Hardcoded Payment Processor Credential — PCI-DSS Req 6.3 — Security Vulnerabilities.
recommendation: Payment processor credentials must be stored in environment variables or a secrets manager, never in source code.

name: Card Data in Application Logs
description: Card Data in Application Logs — PCI-DSS Req 10.2 — Audit Logging.
recommendation: PAN and card data must never appear in logs. Log only masked values (last 4 digits) for audit purposes.

name: Default or Weak Credential
description: Default or Weak Credential — PCI-DSS Req 8.3 — Authentication Management.
recommendation: Default credentials fail PCI-DSS Req 8. Deploy with unique strong credentials and rotate on a defined schedule.

name: Plaintext Card Data Written to File
description: Plaintext Card Data Written to File — PCI-DSS Req 3.5 — Encryption of Stored Data.
recommendation: Stored cardholder data must be encrypted with AES-256. Never write PAN or card data to plaintext files.
compliance_ref: PCI-DSS Req 3.5 — Encryption of Stored Data

name: Missing PCI Scope Isolation
description: Missing PCI Scope Isolation — PCI-DSS Req 12.5 — Scope Management.
recommendation: Ensure cardholder data environment (CDE) systems are isolated from out-of-scope systems. Review network segmentation.

name: Personal Data in Application Logs
description: Personal Data in Application Logs — GDPR Art. 5(1)(f) — Integrity and Confidentiality.
recommendation: Personal data must not appear in logs. Log event IDs only; redact or pseudonymize PII in all log outputs.

name: Third-Party Tracker Without Consent
description: Third-Party Tracker Without Consent — GDPR Art. 7 — Conditions for Consent.
recommendation: Third-party analytics and tracking require explicit prior consent under GDPR. Implement a Consent Management Platform.

name: Personal Data Written to File Unencrypted
description: Personal Data Written to File Unencrypted — GDPR Art. 32 — Security of Processing.
recommendation: Personal data written to files must be encrypted at rest with AES-256. Verify access controls on the file path.

name: IP Address Stored Without Masking
description: IP Address Stored Without Masking — GDPR Art. 5(1)(c) — Data Minimisation.
recommendation: IP addresses are personal data under GDPR. Anonymize the last octet before storage or document the Art. 6 legal basis.

name: Personal Data in Error Messages
description: Personal Data in Error Messages — GDPR Art. 5(1)(f) — Integrity and Confidentiality.
recommendation: Error messages must not expose personal data. Log full detail server-side only; show a generic message to end users.

name: Sensitive PII Field Without Encryption Indicator
description: Sensitive PII Field Without Encryption Indicator — GDPR Art. 32 — Security of Processing.
recommendation: Sensitive personal identifiers must be encrypted or pseudonymized at rest. Use column-level encryption for sensitive fields.

name: Cookie Set Without Consent Check
description: Cookie Set Without Consent Check — GDPR Art. 7 — Conditions for Consent.
recommendation: Non-essential cookies require explicit user consent before setting. Integrate a Consent Management Platform.

name: Personal Data Hashed With Weak Algorithm
description: Personal Data Hashed With Weak Algorithm — GDPR Art. 32 — Security of Processing.
recommendation: MD5/SHA-1 pseudonymization is reversible via rainbow tables. Use SHA-256 with salt, or bcrypt/argon2 for identity fields.

name: Data Transfer to Non-EEA Cloud Service
description: Data Transfer to Non-EEA Cloud Service — GDPR Art. 44 — Transfer to Third Countries.
recommendation: Transferring personal data to non-EEA processors requires SCCs or an adequacy decision. Verify data residency configuration.
compliance_ref: GDPR Art. 44 — Transfer to Third Countries

name: Missing Data Deletion / Expiry Field
description: Missing Data Deletion / Expiry Field — GDPR Art. 5(1)(e) — Storage Limitation.
recommendation: Personal data must not be retained longer than necessary. Add a deleted_at or expires_at field and enforce deletion schedules.

name: Authentication Bypass Flag
description: Authentication Bypass Flag — SOC 2 CC6.1 — Logical Access Controls.
recommendation: Authentication bypass flags must never be deployed. Remove entirely; use environment-gated feature flags.

name: Debug Backdoor or Maintenance Mode
description: Debug Backdoor or Maintenance Mode — SOC 2 CC6.1 — Logical Access Controls.
recommendation: Backdoor and maintenance-mode access paths violate SOC 2 logical access controls. Remove from production code entirely.

name: CORS Wildcard Origin
description: CORS Wildcard Origin — SOC 2 CC6.6 — External Threats.
recommendation: Wildcard CORS grants unrestricted cross-origin access. Restrict to an explicit allow-list of known trusted origins.

name: Insecure Direct Object Reference
description: Insecure Direct Object Reference — SOC 2 CC6.1 — Logical Access Controls.
recommendation: Direct use of user-supplied IDs in queries risks unauthorized data access. Verify record ownership before returning data.

name: Silent Exception Swallowing
description: Silent Exception Swallowing — SOC 2 CC7.2 — System Monitoring.
recommendation: Silent exception handling hides operational failures. Log all exceptions with context and alert on unexpected error rates.

name: Privileged Operation Without Audit Log
description: Privileged Operation Without Audit Log — SOC 2 CC7.3 — Audit Logging.
recommendation: Destructive and privileged operations must produce audit log entries. Log actor, action, timestamp, and affected resource ID.

name: Unrestricted File Upload
description: Unrestricted File Upload — SOC 2 CC6.8 — Input Validation.
recommendation: Unrestricted file uploads enable code execution and storage abuse. Validate type, size, and content before persisting.

name: HTTPS Not Enforced
description: HTTPS Not Enforced — SOC 2 CC6.7 — Transmission Controls.
recommendation: HTTPS must be enforced for all production traffic. Enable SECURE_SSL_REDIRECT and SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE before deployment.

name: Hardcoded Inter-Service Token
description: Hardcoded Inter-Service Token — SOC 2 CC6.3 — Access Provisioning.
recommendation: Inter-service credentials hardcoded in source enable lateral movement. Use a secrets manager or mTLS for service-to-service auth.

name: Test Credentials Left in Code
description: Test Credentials Left in Code — SOC 2 CC6.3 — Access Provisioning.
recommendation: Test credentials in production code violate environment separation. Remove or gate behind strict environment checks.

name: IDOR — Direct Object Reference from Request
description: IDOR — Direct Object Reference from Request — A01:2021 — Broken Access Control.
recommendation: Verify record ownership against the authenticated user before returning the object. Map incoming IDs to a permission check.

name: CORS Wildcard Origin
description: CORS Wildcard Origin — A01:2021 — Broken Access Control.
recommendation: Wildcard CORS grants any origin access. Replace * with an explicit allow-list of trusted origins.

name: Hardcoded Admin/Role Bypass
description: Hardcoded Admin/Role Bypass — A01:2021 — Broken Access Control.
recommendation: Hardcoded role flags in source defeat access control. Use a real RBAC system; remove the literal and load the role from the authenticated session.

name: Route Handler Without Auth Decorator (Flask/FastAPI)
description: Route Handler Without Auth Decorator (Flask/FastAPI) — A01:2021 — Broken Access Control.
recommendation: Sensitive route handler appears to lack an authentication/authorization decorator. Add @login_required / Depends(auth) / equivalent.

name: Weak Hash (MD5/SHA-1) for Sensitive Data
description: Weak Hash (MD5/SHA-1) for Sensitive Data — A02:2021 — Cryptographic Failures.
recommendation: MD5 and SHA-1 are cryptographically broken. Use SHA-256+ for integrity and bcrypt/argon2/scrypt for password storage.

name: Prohibited Weak Cipher
description: Prohibited Weak Cipher — A02:2021 — Cryptographic Failures.
recommendation: DES, 3DES, RC4, RC2, and MD4 are broken or deprecated. Use AES-256-GCM or ChaCha20-Poly1305.

name: Hardcoded Crypto IV or Nonce
description: Hardcoded Crypto IV or Nonce — A02:2021 — Cryptographic Failures.
recommendation: Hardcoded IVs/nonces/salts destroy semantic security and enable replay attacks. Generate a fresh random value per operation.

name: TLS Verification Disabled
description: TLS Verification Disabled — A02:2021 — Cryptographic Failures.
recommendation: Never disable TLS certificate verification. Disabling it exposes all transport data to man-in-the-middle attacks.

name: SQL Injection — String Concatenation in Query
description: SQL Injection — String Concatenation in Query — A03:2021 — Injection.
recommendation: String-formatted SQL queries are injection-prone. Use parameterized queries or an ORM's bound parameters.

name: Command Injection — User Input in exec/popen
description: Command Injection — User Input in exec/popen — A03:2021 — Injection.
recommendation: Concatenating user input into a shell command enables command injection. Use argv arrays and validate/escape inputs, or call the binary directly with arguments.

name: NoSQL Injection — Unparameterized Query
description: NoSQL Injection — Unparameterized Query — A03:2021 — Injection.
recommendation: User-controlled input injected into NoSQL queries can bypass filters and access controls. Use schema validation and sanitization.

name: LDAP Injection
description: LDAP Injection — A03:2021 — Injection.
recommendation: User input concatenated into LDAP filters enables filter injection. Use parameterised LDAP filter construction.

name: XPath Injection
description: XPath Injection — A03:2021 — Injection.
recommendation: String-formatted XPath enables query manipulation. Use bound variables (xpath with a variables map) instead of concatenation.

name: innerHTML / outerHTML / document.write Assignment
description: innerHTML / outerHTML / document.write Assignment — A03:2021 — Injection.
recommendation: Direct DOM assignment of unescaped data is an XSS sink. Set .textContent / use a framework's safe binding, or sanitise via DOMPurify.

name: Debug Mode Enabled
description: Debug Mode Enabled — A05:2021 — Security Misconfiguration.
recommendation: Disable debug mode before deployment. Stack traces and verbose errors leak internals and may allow execution via debug consoles.

name: Verbose Error/Traceback Exposed
description: Verbose Error/Traceback Exposed — A05:2021 — Security Misconfiguration.
recommendation: Returning full tracebacks or exception text to clients leaks internals. Log full detail server-side; show a generic message to users.

name: Default or Weak Credential
description: Default or Weak Credential — A05:2021 — Security Misconfiguration.
recommendation: Default/weak credentials must be replaced before deployment. Rotate on a defined schedule.

name: Weak Session Token Generation (Math.random / random)
description: Weak Session Token Generation (Math.random / random) — A07:2021 — Identification and Authentication Failures.
recommendation: Math.random / Python random are not cryptographically secure. Use crypto.randomUUID(), secrets.token_urlsafe(), or secrets.token_hex() for session tokens.

name: Login Route Without Rate Limiting (heuristic)
description: Login Route Without Rate Limiting (heuristic) — A07:2021 — Identification and Authentication Failures.
recommendation: Login endpoints require rate limiting and account lockout. Add throttling (e.g., slowapi, express-rate-limit) and consider MFA.

name: Insecure Deserialization (Python pickle / marshal)
description: Insecure Deserialization (Python pickle / marshal) — A08:2021 — Software and Data Integrity Failures.
recommendation: pickle/marshal.loads on untrusted data enables arbitrary code execution. Use json or a typed serializer; never unpickle attacker-controlled bytes.
compliance_ref: A08:2021 — Software and Data Integrity Failures

name: Insecure Deserialization (Java ObjectInputStream / JavaScript eval)
description: Insecure Deserialization (Java ObjectInputStream / JavaScript eval) — A08:2021 — Software and Data Integrity Failures.
recommendation: Deserialising untrusted Java objects or evaluating parsed JSON enables RCE/injection. Use allow-list type checks; never eval user data.
compliance_ref: A08:2021 — Software and Data Integrity Failures

name: JWT Verify Disabled / Unsigned Algorithm
description: JWT Verify Disabled / Unsigned Algorithm — A08:2021 — Software and Data Integrity Failures.
recommendation: Disabling JWT signature verification or accepting alg=none allows forged tokens. Always verify with an explicit allow-list of algorithms (e.g., RS256).
compliance_ref: A08:2021 — Software and Data Integrity Failures

name: Curl-Pipe-Shell (Insecure Update/Install)
description: Curl-Pipe-Shell (Insecure Update/Install) — A08:2021 — Software and Data Integrity Failures.
recommendation: Piping a remote download straight to a shell executes whatever the server returns. Download to a file, verify a checksum/signature, then execute.
compliance_ref: A08:2021 — Software and Data Integrity Failures

name: Silent Exception Swallowing
description: Silent Exception Swallowing — A09:2021 — Security Logging and Monitoring Failures.
recommendation: Silent exception handling hides operational and security failures. Log the exception with context; alert on unexpected error rates.
compliance_ref: A09:2021 — Security Logging and Monitoring Failures

name: Privileged Operation Without Audit Log
description: Privileged Operation Without Audit Log — A09:2021 — Security Logging and Monitoring Failures.
recommendation: Destructive and privileged operations must produce audit log entries. Log actor, action, timestamp, and affected resource ID.
compliance_ref: A09:2021 — Security Logging and Monitoring Failures

name: SSRF — User Input in HTTP Client URL
description: SSRF — User Input in HTTP Client URL — A10:2021 — Server-Side Request Forgery.
recommendation: Passing request data directly to an HTTP client enables SSRF. Validate the URL against an allow-list of permitted hosts/schemes before issuing the request.

name: SSRF — User Input in Redirect / File Open
description: SSRF — User Input in Redirect / File Open — A10:2021 — Server-Side Request Forgery.
recommendation: Using request data in redirects, file opens, or send_file allows local-file-read and SSRF. Resolve the path/URL to an absolute, validated target first.

name: Personal Data Written Unencrypted to Disk
description: Personal Data Written Unencrypted to Disk — CIS v8 3.11 (IG1).
recommendation: Sensitive data written to files must be encrypted at rest. Use AES-256 (or column-level encryption) before persisting.

name: Sensitive Field Stored in Plaintext Variable
description: Sensitive Field Stored in Plaintext Variable — CIS v8 3.11 (IG1).
recommendation: Sensitive identifiers must be encrypted or pseudonymised at rest. Mask or hash before storing in memory beyond a single request scope.

name: Debug Mode Enabled in Configuration
description: Debug Mode Enabled in Configuration — CIS v8 4.1 (IG1).
recommendation: Disable debug mode before deployment. Stack traces and debug consoles expose internals and may allow code execution.

name: Default or Vendor Credential
description: Default or Vendor Credential — CIS v8 4.2 (IG1).
recommendation: Default/vendor credentials must be replaced before deployment. Rotate on a defined schedule.

name: TLS Verification Disabled
description: TLS Verification Disabled — CIS v8 4.6 (IG1).
recommendation: Never disable TLS certificate verification. Disabling it exposes transport data to man-in-the-middle attacks.

name: Unencrypted HTTP Endpoint (external)
description: Unencrypted HTTP Endpoint (external) — CIS v8 4.6 (IG1).
recommendation: Replace http:// with https:// for all external endpoints. Plaintext transport exposes data in transit.

name: Hardcoded User Credential
description: Hardcoded User Credential — CIS v8 5.2 (IG1).
recommendation: User credentials must not appear in source. Use environment variables or a secrets manager; rotate any committed value.

name: Generic Account Name (admin/root) Hardcoded
description: Generic Account Name (admin/root) Hardcoded — CIS v8 5.4 (IG1).
recommendation: Hardcoded admin/root accounts in source defeat least-privilege. Use a real user store with role-based provisioning.

name: Authentication Bypass Flag
description: Authentication Bypass Flag — CIS v8 6.8 (IG2).
recommendation: Authentication bypass flags must never be deployed. Remove entirely; use environment-gated feature flags if you need a non-prod override.

name: Debug Backdoor / Maintenance Mode
description: Debug Backdoor / Maintenance Mode — CIS v8 6.8 (IG2).
recommendation: Backdoor and maintenance-mode access paths violate least-privilege. Remove from production code entirely.

name: Insecure Direct Object Reference
description: Insecure Direct Object Reference — CIS v8 6.7 (IG2).
recommendation: Direct use of user-supplied IDs in queries risks unauthorized data access. Verify record ownership before returning data.

name: CORS Wildcard Origin
description: CORS Wildcard Origin — CIS v8 6.7 (IG2).
recommendation: Wildcard CORS grants unrestricted cross-origin access. Restrict to an explicit allow-list of known trusted origins.

name: Silent Exception Swallowing
description: Silent Exception Swallowing — CIS v8 8.2 (IG2).
recommendation: Silent exception handling hides operational failures. Log the exception with context; alert on unexpected error rates.

name: Privileged Operation Without Audit Log
description: Privileged Operation Without Audit Log — CIS v8 8.5 (IG2).
recommendation: Destructive and privileged operations must produce audit log entries. Log actor, action, timestamp, and affected resource ID.

name: Print/Console Logging on Production Path
description: Print/Console Logging on Production Path — CIS v8 8.2 (IG2).
recommendation: Production code should use a structured logger, not print/console. Ensure sensitive values are not passed to the logger.

name: SQL Injection — String Concatenation
description: SQL Injection — String Concatenation — CIS v8 16.10 (IG2).
recommendation: String-formatted SQL queries are injection-prone. Use parameterised queries or an ORM's bound parameters.

name: Command Injection — User Input Concatenated into exec
description: Command Injection — User Input Concatenated into exec — CIS v8 16.10 (IG2).
recommendation: Concatenating user input into a shell command enables command injection. Use argv arrays and validate/escape inputs, or call the binary directly.

name: Insecure Deserialization (Pickle / Marshal / Java ObjectInputStream)
description: Insecure Deserialization (Pickle / Marshal / Java ObjectInputStream) — CIS v8 16.10 (IG2).
recommendation: Deserialising untrusted data enables remote code execution. Use json or a typed serializer; never unpickle attacker-controlled bytes.

name: Path Traversal — User Input in File Path
description: Path Traversal — User Input in File Path — CIS v8 16.10 (IG2).
recommendation: Concatenating user input into a file path enables path traversal. Resolve to an absolute, normalised path and verify it stays within an allow-listed root.

name: Weak Hash (MD5/SHA-1)
description: Weak Hash (MD5/SHA-1) — CIS v8 16.11 (IG2).
recommendation: MD5 and SHA-1 are cryptographically broken. Use SHA-256+ for integrity and bcrypt/argon2/scrypt for password storage.

name: Prohibited Weak Cipher
description: Prohibited Weak Cipher — CIS v8 16.11 (IG2).
recommendation: DES, 3DES, RC4, RC2, and MD4 are broken or deprecated. Use AES-256-GCM or ChaCha20-Poly1305.

name: innerHTML / document.write (XSS sink)
description: innerHTML / document.write (XSS sink) — CIS v8 16.10 (IG2).
recommendation: Direct DOM assignment of unescaped data is an XSS sink. Set .textContent / use a framework's safe binding, or sanitise via DOMPurify.

name: SSRF — User Input in HTTP Client URL
description: SSRF — User Input in HTTP Client URL — CIS v8 16.10 (IG2).
recommendation: Passing request data directly to an HTTP client enables SSRF. Validate the URL against an allow-list of permitted hosts/schemes.

name: Open Redirect — User Input in redirect()
description: Open Redirect — User Input in redirect() — CIS v8 16.10 (IG2).
recommendation: Redirecting to a user-supplied URL enables phishing chains. Validate the target against an allow-list or use indirect references.

name: Hardcoded Inter-Service / API Token
description: Hardcoded Inter-Service / API Token — CIS v8 16.14 (IG2).
recommendation: Inter-service credentials hardcoded in source enable lateral movement. Use a secrets manager or mTLS for service-to-service auth.

name: JWT Token in Source
description: Potential secret detected: JWT Token in Source. This may be a hardcoded credential.
recommendation: JWTs embedded in source are valid credentials. Move signing keys to a secrets manager; rotate any committed token.

name: Azure Storage Connection String
description: Potential secret detected: Azure Storage Connection String. This may be a hardcoded credential.
recommendation: Azure Storage account keys in source grant full read/write to the account. Use SAS tokens or Azure AD with managed identity.

name: Google Cloud API Key
description: Potential secret detected: Google Cloud API Key. This may be a hardcoded credential.
recommendation: Google Cloud API keys in source grant access to the enabled GCP APIs. Restrict by HTTP referrer/IP, then move to a secrets manager.

name: OpenAI API Key
description: Potential secret detected: OpenAI API Key. This may be a hardcoded credential.
recommendation: OpenAI API keys in source grant access to your OpenAI account and billable usage. Move to environment variables or a secrets manager; rotate.

name: Anthropic API Key
description: Potential secret detected: Anthropic API Key. This may be a hardcoded credential.
recommendation: Anthropic API keys in source grant access to your Claude account. Move to environment variables or a secrets manager; rotate.

name: Heroku API Key
description: Potential secret detected: Heroku API Key. This may be a hardcoded credential.
recommendation: Heroku API keys grant full account access. Move to environment variables or a secrets manager.

name: Slack Incoming Webhook URL
description: Potential secret detected: Slack Incoming Webhook URL. This may be a hardcoded credential.
recommendation: Slack incoming webhooks in source allow anyone to post into the channel. Store in env vars; treat as semi-secret and rotate if exposed.

name: Mailgun API Key
description: Potential secret detected: Mailgun API Key. This may be a hardcoded credential.
recommendation: Mailgun API keys allow sending email as your domain. Move to environment variables or a secrets manager.

name: PHI Field Assignment Without Encryption Indicator
description: PHI Field Assignment Without Encryption Indicator — §164.312(a)(2)(iii) — Encryption.
recommendation: PHI assignment without a visible encryption step is likely plaintext storage. Wrap in an AES/cipher helper before assignment or storage.

name: No Audit Log on Authentication Event
description: No Audit Log on Authentication Event — §164.308(a)(6) — Security Incident Procedures.
recommendation: Authentication events are reportable security incidents and must be logged. Emit an audit log entry on success and failure.

name: Backup Routine Without Encryption Indicator
description: Backup Routine Without Encryption Indicator — §164.308(a)(7) — Contingency Plan.
recommendation: Backups containing ePHI must be encrypted at rest and stored with restricted access. Verify your backup pipeline uses encrypted storage.

name: Test Card Number in Source
description: Test Card Number in Source — PCI-DSS Req 6.4.3 — Production Data Not Used in Testing.
recommendation: Well-known test card numbers in production code can be confused with real PANs. Use the official processor test numbers behind a strict environment check.
compliance_ref: PCI-DSS Req 6.4.3 — Production Data Not Used in Testing

name: CSRF Protection Disabled
description: CSRF Protection Disabled — PCI-DSS Req 6.5 — Cross-Site Request Forgery.
recommendation: CSRF protection must be enabled on all state-changing endpoints. Use synchronizer tokens, SameSite cookies, or double-submit cookies.

name: Missing Right-to-Erasure Implementation
description: Missing Right-to-Erasure Implementation — GDPR Art. 17 — Right to Erasure.
recommendation: Delete handlers must anonymise, not just remove, personal data from backups and downstream systems. Implement a verified erasure flow.

name: Third-Party SDK With Personal Data
description: Third-Party SDK With Personal Data — GDPR Art. 28 — Processor Obligations.
recommendation: Sending personal identifiers to third-party analytics requires a Data Processing Agreement and a legal basis. Verify DPA exists before identifying users.

name: MFA Bypass Flag
description: MFA Bypass Flag — SOC 2 CC6.1 — Logical Access Controls.
recommendation: MFA bypass flags must never be deployed. Remove entirely; use environment-gated feature flags if you need a non-prod override.

name: Security Header Disabled
description: Security Header Disabled — SOC 2 CC6.6 — External Threats.
recommendation: Security headers protect against clickjacking, MIME sniffing, and protocol downgrade. Re-enable each header at the framework or proxy layer.
